fields.headline: Rooted in Italy. Grown in Santa Barbara.
fields.lede: Limited-production estate wines from Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, inspired by generations of tradition.

blocks.body:
From one of the most beautiful vineyard estates in California comes a collection of limited-production wines from Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara. Crafted by acclaimed Santa Barbara winemaker Douglas Margerum, these wines reflect remarkable terroir, patient farming, and restrained, site-driven winemaking.

Set against the rolling hills of eastern Santa Barbara County, the estate vineyard is planted with Italian and Bordeaux varietals ideally suited to the warm days and cool evenings of Happy Canyon. The dramatic landscape, mineral-rich soils, and extended growing season produce wines of notable depth, structure, and elegance.

At Santi Rosina, we believe great wine is rooted in heritage, shaped by place, and meant to bring people together. From our estate in Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, we grow Italian and Bordeaux varietals, honoring generations of family tradition while embracing the character of California. Every bottle reflects our commitment to craftsmanship, authenticity, and creating wines that inspire connection around the table.
Produced in small quantities and available through our wine club and select restaurant partners, these wines are made to be shared around a table, aged in a cellar, and revisited across vintages.

fields.title: Our Story
fields.intro: Every great wine has a place it comes from, and a place it's meant to take you.

blocks.body: Santi Rosina was created from the belief that the best things in life are cultivated slowly. Meals that linger around the table. Vineyards tended by hand. Recipes refined over generations. A deep love for the land and for the people gathered around it.

When we discovered this hidden valley in Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, it felt less like somewhere new and more like somewhere familiar, a landscape that could have been lifted from the Italian countryside. The name Santi Rosina honors that connection: a family's Italian roots, carried across generations and planted in California soil.

Here, Italian and Bordeaux varietals grow side by side. Sangiovese and Nebbiolo share the vineyard with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, bringing together two great wine traditions in one remarkable estate. A meeting of Old World patience and California possibility, where heritage and innovation exist in harmony.

Olive trees, orchards, fields of lavender and sunflowers, and open pasture share the landscape, creating an estate reminiscent of Tuscany. The same soil that nourishes the vines supports everything grown here, reflecting a philosophy that great wine belongs next to great food and good living.

Every decision is intentional. Every vine is tended by hand. Every bottle is crafted with patience rather than haste. Not because it is the easiest path, but because it is the one that produces wines with authenticity, depth, and a sense of place.

Santi Rosina is an expression of two worlds brought together on a single hillside. Italian soul. California terroir. Wines created to be shared around a table where conversation lasts into the evening and every glass invites another story.

At Santi Rosina, we believe great wine is rooted in heritage, shaped by place, and meant to bring people together. From our estate in Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, we grow Italian and Bordeaux varietals, honoring generations of family tradition while embracing the character of California. Every bottle reflects our commitment to craftsmanship, authenticity, and creating wines that inspire connection around the table.

items.name: Doug Margerum
items.bio:
For more than forty years, Doug Margerum has been one of the defining figures of Santa Barbara wine. He fell for wine as a child, traveling through France with his parents, and grew up working in restaurants. In 1981, the year he graduated from UC Santa Barbara, his family bought the Wine Cask. Over the next 26 years he built it into one of California’s most respected wine destinations. In 1994 it won *Wine Spectator*’s Grand Award, one of only 74 restaurants worldwide to earn it that year. His Wine Cask Futures program, launched in 1984, helped bring Santa Barbara wines to a national audience. He was also the first to bring producers like Didier Dagueneau, René Geoffroy and Dominique Laurent to the United States.

In 1986, Doug co-founded Vita Nova with Bob Lindquist of Qupé and Jim Clendenen of Au Bon Climat. In 2001 he started Margerum Wine Company in a 240-square-foot space behind Brander Vineyard. It has since grown into one of the county’s most celebrated wineries, alongside his Barden label from the Sta. Rita Hills and his 18-acre Margerum Estate planted to Rhône varieties.

His years tasting the great wines of Europe shaped a simple philosophy: balance over power, and place over technique. That conviction is the foundation of Santi Rosina. In Happy Canyon, Doug makes wines from Bordeaux and Italian varieties: ripe enough to show California sunshine, yet restrained enough to honor the classics that inspired them.

He has also consulted for Chêne Bleu in France and has served on the Smithsonian’s Kitchen Cabinet and the advisory board of the Julia Child Foundation.

items.name: Robert Daugherty
items.bio:
Robert’s understanding of and interest in winemaking took root at an early age, when he worked alongside his aunt and uncle, Diana and Rick Longoria, the owners and winemakers of Longoria Wines, one of Santa Barbara County’s legendary wineries. Under their mentorship, he learned the art of making elegant, handcrafted, food-friendly wines. After graduating from college, Robert lived in Europe, where he deepened his passion for wines from around the world. He then spent two harvests in New Zealand, where he learned larger-scale winemaking.

Back in California, he spent four years on the cellar and viticulture team at Dierberg and Star Lane, working with fruit from Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, the Sta. Rita Hills and the Santa Maria Valley. He then joined Winc as a start-up and helped it grow significantly. Since 2023 Robert has been head winemaker at Margerum Wine Company, where he oversees small-batch winemaking.

items.name: Ben Merz
items.bio:
Ben Merz joined Coastal Vineyard Care Associates after graduating from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo with a degree in viticulture and agribusiness. Since then he has become one of Santa Barbara County’s most respected viticulturists. He is known for a hands-on approach in the vineyard and for the lasting relationships he has built with growers, winemakers and industry professionals across the region.

Ben and his team at Coastal have played a pivotal role in the growth of Santa Barbara County’s wine region. They farm and source fruit from many of the county’s most reputable sites. Few people know Santa Barbara County’s vineyards as well, from block to block and from season to season.

At Santi Rosina, Ben brings that same care to the vineyard in Happy Canyon. There, warm days and cool nights let Bordeaux and Italian varieties ripen fully while keeping their freshness and structure. His farming reflects the estate’s belief that great wine begins in the vineyard: balanced vines, careful timing and fruit that speaks clearly of its place.

items.name: Juve Buenrostro
items.bio: Juve brings more than two decades of experience in vineyard work and management in the Santa Ynez Valley. His deep knowledge of the valley’s vineyards and his patient attention to detail make him an invaluable part of our team. Juve makes sure every grape reaches its fullest potential, capturing the terroir of the Santa Ynez Valley in every bottle.

blocks.heading: Vineyard Team
blocks.body: During harvest, our vineyard crew is in the rows by 2 a.m., picking every cluster by hand. Picking in the cool of night keeps the fruit fresh and bright, so it reaches the winery in perfect condition. With more than 100 years of combined experience, this team knows every vine, every block and every season. Their skill and dedication are the foundation of every bottle we make.
